then.text: That's the only page I found. Unless you count the beer mats with phone numbers on them. Which I don't.

else.text: A page of a monk's book? Funny you should say. This blew in the door on Tuesday on a gust and landed on the bar. I thought it was the menu.
Old Irish writing, little drawings of birds in the margins. Somebody's been doodling in church. Here, take it. Monks were always welcome at Blakes.
{player} tucks the vellum page carefully into the Fieldbook.
{greeting} Welcome to Blakes of the Hollow. The bar's hardly changed since the 1880s, and neither have some of the customers.
The Hollow's the dip in the street outside. When it rains, the street comes in to visit. We give it a stool.

en_quizmaster.text: {greeting} Quiz night at Blakes. Five questions, no phones, and no conferring with the fella at the end of the bar, because he's wrong.

else.text: Fair enough. Come back when you've read up on your eels.

en_regular.text: {greeting} Boxty on the griddle, boxty in the pan. Have you had boxty yet? You haven't lived. You've existed, at most.
It's potato pancake. Grated raw spud and mashed spud together. Two kinds of potato in the one dish. That's how you know you're in Fermanagh.

enniskillen_blakes_darts.text: Board's in the corner, darts are in the tin, and the oche is that bit of tape the cleaner keeps trying to lift.
